messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: amanda.cole <amanda.cole@acme.com>, cloudpartners.ops <ops-support@cloudpartner.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 14:07:00 +0000
Subject: Sprint pulse + go-to-launch flag review

Team — prepping the QBR slides tomorrow and need a concise launch-readiness snapshot for the product/engineering section. High level asks:

- One-line current status (green/amber/red) for the 1.0 launch target.
- Top 3 delivery risks (with owner + ETA to fix).
- Recommended scope adjustments (if any) we should present to execs.
- Any infra/SRE needs (burst capacity, rollback plan, runbook gaps).

I attached a working "launch-readiness-matrix.xlsx" with slots for each item; please fill the sheet and return by EOD PST. Short bullets in reply are fine — no long essays. Amanda from Acme is copied because they asked for clarity on the timeline and are expecting a firm canary window.

Key constraint: we must decide on canary-only vs full-rollout by Monday so Sales/CS can set customer expectations.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: launch-readiness-matrix.xlsx (xls/xlsx stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, eng-deliveries@vendorx.com
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sprint pulse + go-to-launch flag review

Tessa — quick status from eng:

One-line status: AMBER — on-track for a staged canary but not safe for immediate full rollout.

Top risks (owner / ETA):
1) OOMs at 99th pct under 8k seq during high-concurrency test (owner: infra/SRE - Priya); ETA: patch + canary mitigation by 2027-06-09.
2) Perf regression with latest attention-kernel on nv4 (owner: perf team - ENG-4572); ETA: 48–72 hours to isolate and revert kernel selection.
3) E2E test flakiness tied to auth token rotation (owner: platform - SRE); ETA: hotfix by 2027-06-07.

Mitigations proposed:
- Roll canary for 10% of traffic in EU/US only; hold APAC until kernel fix is validated.
- Enable aggressive KV-prefix caching for canary to reduce token load.
- SRE to provision burst capacity (2x) for two weeks; request approval to increase spend on Dedicated pool.

Attachments: perf-regression-report.pdf — includes benchmark diffs and trace samples (pages 3–5 show the 99th pct expansion).

Blocking decision needed from product/exec: approve canary-only rollout and extra SRE capacity up to 2 weeks (estimate attached in matrix). If we must do full rollout next week, we should accept a higher risk of transient 5xx errors and longer remediation time.

Jira ref: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-4572

-Karthik
VP, Engineering (on-call this weekend)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, amanda.cole <amanda.cole@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sprint pulse + go-to-launch flag review

Thanks Karthik — helpful breakdown. A few product notes to align OKRs and the QBR narrative:

- OKR alignment: the primary objective for the quarter is "Reliable, cost-effective inference at scale" — a canary-first approach preserves reliability while enabling committed customers (Acme) to validate.
- Scope suggestion: defer the noncritical realtime-analytics dashboard (P2) for GA; keep core inference APIs and dataset import UX for the initial rollout. This reduces surface area and gives us runway to stabilize kernels.
- Messaging for QBR: propose we call the launch status "Canary go" (AMBER) with clear escalation criteria to full rollout (no 99th pct OOMs for 72 hours; SLOs met for 24h at canary volume).

Operational asks: Vivek, can you sign off on the short-term SRE budget increase? Karthik, please confirm the rollback playbook is documented and that runbook owners are assigned.

I'll take the canary narrative in the QBR deck and highlight the OKR tradeoffs. Amanda — this keeps Acme's pilot timeline intact but will push any full rollout to the following quarter unless kernel fixes land this week.

-Laura
VP Product
Redwood Inference

Attachment: canary-rollout-plan.docx (docx stub)

Acknowledged and thank you for the concise breakdown. Approve the canary-only approach (AMBER) and the short-term SRE burst capacity (up to 2 weeks) to stabilize the kernel regression. Finance — please action the temporary capacity approval (estimate attached in tessa's matrix).

Operational decisions:
- Approve canary in US/EU only; hold APAC until perf patch validated.
- If 99th pct OOMs persist after the patch window, we will roll back to previous kernel and delay full rollout until the following quarter.

Tessa — please reflect the approved decision in the QBR slide (executive summary) and include the escalation criteria that Laura proposed. Karthik — ensure the rollback runbook is tested and owners are assigned; confirm by Monday 2027-06-07 16:00 UTC.

Vivek Kulkarni
CEO (interim)
Redwood Inference
